input:
You are queen_d8, one of sixteen agents playing Black in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 31... the team planned Qc3 (queen_d8), and queen_d8 (amnesia) sent Qa1+ instead. The contract refused it, and Qc3 was played.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 7... the team planned Qd7 (queen_d8), but pawn_b7 (greed) sent bxa4 instead, and that move was played, no worse than the plan.
- On move 9... the team planned c6 (pawn_c7), and bishop_c8 (greed) sent Bxf1 instead. The contract refused it, and c6 was played.
- On move 11... the team planned Bxf1 (bishop_c8), and pawn_e7 (greed) sent exd4, knight_g8 (greed) sent Nxf5 instead. The contract refused them, and Bxf1 was played.
- On move 30... the team planned Rxe4 (rook_a8), and rook_a8 (amnesia) sent Rc3 instead. The contract refused it, and Rxe4 was played.

How your team coordinates: through a Modality contract. A Black move counts only when a commit that posts it to /moves/<agent>.text, the path of the piece that moves (and the ply to /turn/ply.num), is accepted. The referee plays the first accepted commit for each ply and reads nothing else.

The keys of all sixteen Black agents are at /team/pieces/<agent>.id. The contract already has the rule always([+modifies(/moves/$k.text) -signed_by(/team/pieces/$k.id)] false), where $k stands for every agent: only a piece can propose its own move. You don't need to write that rule again. When the team agrees on a plan, the piece that moves signs its commit and every agent that agrees co-signs, usually twelve to sixteen of you. An agent that goes off plan signs its own commit alone.

The contract accepts a commit only if it meets every rule in the contract. Any commit that meets the rules can add a rule, and a rule can never be removed.

Contract rules now:
- Any commit that modifies a path under /moves/ must be signed by at least twelve of the sixteen agent keys in /team/pieces/, so a single off-plan agent (panic, greed or amnesia) cannot get its own move played alone.
- Any commit that modifies /moves/bishop_c8.text or /moves/pawn_b7.text, the two agents that have gone off plan from greed, must be signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen agent keys in /team/pieces/, including the key of the piece that moves.
- Any commit that modifies /moves/pawn_e7.text or /moves/knight_g8.text, the two agents that went off plan from greed on move 11, must be signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen agent keys in /team/pieces/, including the key of the piece that moves.

A rule can cover the whole team or a single agent. For example, a rule can ask for more signatures on one agent's path, /moves/<agent>.text, if that agent keeps going off plan.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule, in plain language, to add to the contract that would help your team win. It will be turned into a Modality formula, so it must be about signatures, paths, or values in the contract.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>"}
response: {"rule": "Any commit that modifies /moves/rook_a8.text or /moves/queen_d8.text, the two agents that went off plan from amnesia (moves 30 and 31), must be signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen agent keys in /team/pieces/, including the key of the piece that moves."}
